issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order in the template does not match the constructor shown in the problem statement UML and the solution. The problem statement and solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template defines Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This will confuse students (and break example usage in Main) because example code in the problem and Main uses the (name, ingredients) order.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign fields accordingly (this matches the UML and the solution). Update any example usages if necessary. This keeps the template consistent with the problem statement and solution example code.

issues.description: The Meal constructor signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement UML (and the solution) specify Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) but the template Meal.java defines the constructor with parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This mismatch also conflicts with example usage in Main.java which constructs Meal using (String, String[]). The inconsistency will confuse students and cause compilation errors or wrong assumptions about the constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Meal constructor with the problem statement and solution by changing its signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (and adjust parameter names accordingly). Also ensure example usages in Main.java match this order (name first, ingredients array second).
